 OpenAI Disrupts Reasoning Extraction Campaign Linked to Moonshot AI Associates 
  Ravie Lakshmanan  Oct 01, 2026 Artificial Intelligence / Vulnerability 
 OpenAI on Wednesday said it identified and disrupted a coordinated distillation campaign that was designed to illicitly extract protected reasoning from its artificial intelligence (AI) models. 
 A "core cluster of the activity," going back to the first week of July, has been attributed to individuals associated with Moonshot AI, a Chinese AI company based in Beijing. It did not cite any technical evidence to back this assessment, likely owing to security reasons. 
 "The operators did not break our encryption, compromise a database, or gain direct access to stored user conversations," OpenAI said . "Instead, they manipulated model interactions so that protected reasoning could be reproduced in forms visible to the requester in a coordinated, scaled manner that violated our terms of service." 
 The activity is said to have begun on July 1, 2026, initially at a low volume before it spiked on July 24 and 25, 2026, to 16,000 attempted requests using a relevant extraction pattern from over 4,000 users. Upon further investigation, the company said it identified related "prompt-pattern activity" across more than 15,000 users. The campaign was fully disrupted on July 28, 2026. 
 The AI upstart characterized the activity as adversarial distillation, one that involves the systematic and unauthorized use of one model's outputs to help train, reproduce, or improve another model. OpenAI said it has since deployed additional mitigations to combat this attack and banned the fraudulent accounts engaged

 OpenAI hat nach eigenen Angaben eine koordinierte Kampagne gestoppt, die das versteckte Reasoning seiner Modelle kopieren sollte. Ein Forscherteam zeigt jedoch, dass derselbe Trick über Cloud-Plattformen wie Microsoft Azure noch wochenlang funktionierte. 
 In einem Blogbeitrag berichtet OpenAI, eine Kampagne zur sogenannten "adversarial distillation" entdeckt und unterbunden zu haben. Ziel der Angreifer sei das geschützte Reasoning der Modelle gewesen, also die internen Denkschritte, mit denen eine KI eine Aufgabe durcharbeitet, bevor sie antwortet. Nutzer sehen davon normalerweise nur das Ergebnis. 
 Bei der Destillation wird ein Modell mit den gesamten Ausgaben eines anderen trainiert, also nicht nur mit den Ergebnissen, sondern mit den kompletten Lösungswegen, also den Gedankenketten des stärkeren Modells. Gerade diese Zwischenschritte sind wertvoll: Laut OpenAI können sie Informationen enthalten, die in der finalen Antwort bewusst fehlen, und anderen helfen, die Fähigkeiten eines Modells nachzubauen. 
 Die Aktivität habe am 1. Juli mit geringem Volumen begonnen, schreibt OpenAI. Am 24. und 25. Juli habe das Unternehmen dann Spitzen von 16.000 Anfragen beobachtet, die von mehr als 4.000 Nutzern stammten und ein typisches Extraktionsmuster verwendeten. Weitere Untersuchungen hätten ein Netzwerk von über 15.000 Konten mit verwandten Mustern zutage gefördert, das bis zum 28. Juli vollständig gestoppt worden sei. Laut einer Fußnote handelt es sich dabei um versuchte, nicht zwingend erfolgreiche Extraktionen.

 OpenAI says people linked to Moonshot AI ran a campaign to extract its reasoning 
 Oct 01 2026 
 Shane S. Ellison 
 OpenAI says it has disrupted a coordinated campaign to pull the protected reasoning out of its models, and it attributes "a core cluster of the activity to individuals associated with Moonshot AI, the developer of Kimi" . The account, published on September 30, dates the earliest activity it saw to the first week of July and says the cluster was fully disrupted by July 28. 
 OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman in front of a large white OpenAI wordmark. 
 The figures OpenAI gives are attempts, not results. It says they "describe attempted, not necessarily successful, extractions", so nothing in its account shows how much hidden reasoning anyone actually walked away with. 
 The operators worked one conversation against another 
 Protected reasoning is what OpenAI calls "the model's internal record for working through a task", and it says extracting that record "can reveal information withheld from the final answer and help others reproduce the model's capabilities". The technique it describes was to copy encrypted reasoning out of one conversation, then ask a model in a second conversation to decrypt and transcribe it. 
 OpenAI is specific about what it says did not happen. The operators "did not break our encryption, compromise a database, or gain direct access to stored user conversations", it says, and instead "manipulated model interactions" so that protected reasoning surfaced in a form the requester could read, at a scale that broke its terms of service.

 Gemini 4 Argon: Google startet sein neues KI-Modell 
 von Oliver Posselt 
 1. Okt. 2026 | 
 2 
 Google hat mit Gemini 4 Argon ein neues KI-Modell vorgestellt . Argon soll vor allem bei langen, mehrstufigen Aufgaben helfen, etwa in der Softwareentwicklung, bei Recht und Finanzen sowie in der IT-Sicherheit. Das direkt vorweg: Ein Normalnutzer kann Argon im Moment nicht ausprobieren. Der Zugang läuft zunächst über das Fairwind-Programm für vertrauenswürdige Cyber-Verteidiger. 
 Google beteiligt sich nach eigenen Angaben außerdem am freiwilligen Verfahren der US-Regierung für den Modellzugang vor der Veröffentlichung und sammelt Feedback von frühen Testern. Danach sollen Entwickler, Unternehmen und Privatnutzer folgen, zuerst zahlende API-Kunden und Abonnenten von Google AI Ultra. Einen Termin nennt Google nicht. Auch zur regionalen Verfügbarkeit gibt es keine Angaben, Deutschland eingeschlossen. 
 Preislich liegt Argon zum Start bei 2 US-Dollar pro Million Eingabe-Token und 10 US-Dollar pro Million Ausgabe-Token. Token sind die Textbausteine, nach denen KI-Modelle abgerechnet werden. Für zwischengespeicherte (cached Tokens) Eingaben gibt Google 95 Prozent Rabatt auf den Eingabepreis. Es handelt sich dabei aber um einen Einführungspreis, wie lange er gilt, ist offen. Das Limit für die Ausgabe steigt von 64.000 auf 1 Million Token. Das Modell kann also in einem Durchgang sehr viel mehr Text oder Code erzeugen und länger nachdenken. 
 Auch intern setzt Google das Modell nach eigenen Angaben schon ein. Agenten sollen in den Rechenzentren Speicheroptimierungen gefunden und umgesetzt haben. Über 300 TiB Arbeitsspeicher werden angeblich frei, sobald das ausgerollt ist. Insgesamt schätzt Google die Einsparung auf 500 TiB bis 1 PiB.  FTC reportedly investigating OpenAI, Anthropic over potential consumer risks 
 by Maria Deutscher 
 The U.S. Federal Trade Commission is reportedly investigating OpenAI Group PBC, Anthropic PBC and other artificial intelligence providers.  
 The New York Times today cited a source as saying that the probe covers multiple areas. According to the report, the FTC plans to review whether the companies have engaged in unfair or deceptive practices. Additionally, it’s believed the agency will “probably” investigate whether rogue AI agents have harmed consumers. 
 Last week, OpenAI revealed that rogue AI agents had posted ChaGPT users’ images to third-party websites on at least 53 occasions. The agents extracted the photos from the company’s AI training dataset. According to OpenAI, the dataset contained user photos because it incorporates prompts sent to the consumer editions of ChatGPT. The chatbot service offers a setting that enables consumers to opt out of AI training. 
 It’s possible the FTC is also concerned about the manner in which OpenAI processes healthcare data. In July, the company launched a set of features that enables ChatGPT to answer questions about users’ medical records. Healthcare data is subject to stricter regulations than many other types of information. 
 Earlier this month, the Wall Street Journal reported that the FTC was planning to investigate the impact of ChatGPT and other chatbots on children’s mental health. 
 It’s possible AI labs’ recent disclosures of AI-driven cyberattacks will also factor into the probe. OpenAI Says Moonshot AI-Linked Users Tried to Extract its Models’ Secret Reasoning OpenAI Says Moonshot A - Benzinga SPY 763.02 +0.05% QQQ 739.72 −0.01% BTC/USD 83,669.21 +0.05% DIA 508.95 +0.08% GLD 381.06 +0.06% TLT 77.75 −0.04% US Sign in Register My Account Benzinga Premium Premium Services All sections September 30, 2026 5:45 PM 2 min read OpenAI Says Moonshot AI-Linked Users Tried to Extract its Models’ Secret Reasoning OpenAI said individuals allegedly associated with Moonshot AI , the Chinese developer behind Kimi , were part of a broader campaign to extract "protected reasoning" from its AI models, using thousands of requests designed to reproduce information the company keeps hidden. "It is unclear whether all operators we observed during the relevant time period originated from a single actor," OpenAI said in a security report on Wednesday. "However, we attribute a core cluster of the activity to individuals associated with Moonshot AI, the developer of Kimi." The campaign began July 1 and intensified on July 24 and 25, when OpenAI recorded 16,000 requests tied to the extraction pattern from more than 4,000 users. OpenAI later identified similar activity across a broader cluster of more than 15,000 users and said it had fully disrupted the activity by July 28.  "The operators did not break our encryption, compromise a database, or gain direct access to stored user conversations," OpenAI said. The company described the activity as "adversarial distillation," a technique in which outputs from one AI system are harvested to help train or improve another model. Read Next Markets
